Practice 04

An institutional co-founder takes a venture from validation to capital readiness and shares the risk through equity.

In short

HAYKALAH builds ventures as an institutional co-founder. We validate the idea, form the company and obtain its approvals, build the platform with partners, prepare the go-to-market and make the company ready for investors. Part of our reward is equity that vests as the venture passes agreed gates. The practice serves founders, private investors and international companies building in the Kingdom. The archive census counts 108 ventures, NewCos and platforms, and HAYKALAH’s own ventures include Arsann (sold in 2023), AS3A (operating) and AGTI. (AI precision farming).

What we do

  • Validation: market research, a feasibility study and HOAM screening.

  • Company formation and setup: commercial registration, sector approvals and Saudization planning.

  • Platform and technology build, in-house and with partners.

  • Go-to-market: pricing, a sales playbook and the first client agreements.

  • Capital readiness: a three-statement model, valuation, due-diligence report, investor pack and data room.

  • Governance: shareholders’ agreements, boards and trackers for conditions precedent.

  • Equity-for-build terms, with partner equity vesting at milestones.

How we create value

  • 01

    Innovation

    We design new ventures as an institutional co-founder: the company, the platform built in-house and with partners, and equity-for-build terms that vest at agreed gates.

  • 06

    Commercialization

    We take a venture from validation through go-to-market to capital readiness, as with Arsann, the parking operator that HAYKALAH’s founder established, built and sold in 2023.

How we work

  1. 01

    Screen

    HOAM compares the opportunity with two decades of precedent before time or capital is spent.

  2. 02

    Validate

    Market research, a feasibility study and a financial model test demand and economics.

  3. 03

    Form and set the gates

    The company is formed and equity vesting is tied to milestones, for example 20% at registration, 30% at the first revenue contract and 50% at an agreed KPI threshold.

  4. 04

    Build and launch

    Platform, team and first clients, with dashboards live from day one.

  5. 05

    Raise, scale or exit

    Kill criteria are agreed at the start, so each gate ends in a clear decision.

Questions

What is an institutional co-founder?

A firm that joins a venture as a founding partner. It brings structuring, governance, capital readiness and relationships, and takes part of its reward in equity rather than in fees alone.

How does equity-for-build work?

The co-founder’s equity vests in stages tied to milestones, such as registration, the first revenue contract and a KPI threshold. Equity for a milestone that is not reached does not vest.

What is HOAM?

The HAYKALAH Opportunity Assessment Matrix. It scores a new opportunity on six axes and compares it with two decades of precedent. It is a screening tool, not investment advice.

Has HAYKALAH taken a venture through to exit?

Yes. Arsann grew from a 2010 parking study into an operating company that was sold to a Saudi investment group in 2023.

Can a foreign company build a venture in Saudi Arabia with HAYKALAH?

Yes. In a localization structure HAYKALAH co-founds the Saudi entity, and its equity vests as the entity registers, wins its first contract and reaches agreed KPIs.

Bring us the idea, the plan or the company you have started. We can start under an NDA.
